A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Intent3D dataset and IntentNet method. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite reformatting and expanded supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original validation/test experiments, component ablations and qualitative results, including the appendix comparison against GPT-4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a human assessment of generated sentences, qualitative evaluations and training curves.

M1.justification: IntentNet retains its backbones, attention architecture, candidate-box matching, verb-object alignment, cascaded loss weighting and inference procedure. The newly described scene-graph organization and detailed network diagram document the existing pipeline without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The 44,990-text, 209-class, 1,042-scene benchmark remains unchanged. Appendix A.8 adds qualitative inference examples involving categories with at least six instances in a scene, extending evaluation to conditions excluded by the dataset's scene-level object-selection rule.

E2.justification: Appendix A.7 adds EDA supplied with ground-truth object candidates as a comparator in qualitative failure-case analyses. Earlier qualitative analyses used IntentNet, its ablations and ground truth. The quantitative comparator sets remain unchanged, including GPT-4, which already appeared in v2's appendix.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a naturalness assessment using 500 randomly selected GPT responses and three PhD evaluators, plus qualitative comparisons giving EDA ground-truth candidates. The original benchmark splits, training budgets, checkpoint-selection rule and Top1-Accuracy/AP metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary analysis expands substantially in scope: A.5 assesses linguistic naturalness, A.7 examines distracting secondary actions, A.8 tests grounding in scenes with numerous same-category objects, and A.10 examines convergence. A.9 adds an object-frequency histogram. The original component ablations and ambiguity examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new human assessment specifies three evaluators but supplies no agreement statistics or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5 retain their numerical results; IntentNet's validation/test AP@0.5 remains 25.36/27.60. Added findings include all 500 sampled responses meeting human-like criteria, secondary-action failures, successful crowded-scene examples, object-frequency statistics and convergence curves. These supplement rather than revise the benchmark results.

T1.justification: The task definition, losses in Equations 1–3 and cascaded adaptive-weighting formula are mathematically unchanged. v3 adds no theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same new task, Intent3D benchmark, baseline evaluation and IntentNet contribution. v3 explicitly mentions state-of-the-art performance in its contribution summary, reiterating the superiority already claimed and reported in v2 without broadening its scope.

C2.justification: A.7 newly explains how secondary actions can distract IntentNet from the primary intention. A.8 discusses applicability beyond the scene-level object-count filter, and A.10 interprets the learning curves as convergence evidence. Earlier limitations concerning GPT subjectivity, annotation ambiguity and missed instances remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies code/project links and documents the JSON scene-graph fields used during dataset construction. However, it removes v2's specifications that Chat-3D-v2 fine-tunes the last two Vicuna layers plus linear layers and starts from the 'Step 3: Scene-level Alignment' checkpoint. These are documentation changes, not demonstrated experimental changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds literature supporting LLM-based annotation, including 3D-GRAND, ScanEnts3D and annotation studies/surveys, plus a robot demonstration motivating intention understanding. It removes some broad background citations, including Flamingo and BLIP-2. The central positioning relative to visual grounding and affordance understanding remains.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits and condenses passages, presents verb-object alignment as three explicit steps, revises the contribution summary and organizes the former supplementary sections under Appendix A. The main section sequence and most explanations remain recognizable; affiliation, conference-header and acknowledgment text also change.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICLR formatting, substantially changing typography, spacing and display placement, with highlighted IntentNet table rows. Figure 2 relabels the initial stage as scene-graph construction. New Figures 8–17 provide failure and crowded-scene examples, denser statistics, training curves and a detailed network diagram; earlier displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes dataset quality and model boundaries easier to assess through the human audit, distraction failures, crowded-scene examples and clearer pipeline/network documentation. Code/project links also improve access information. These gains are limited: the audit lacks an explicit rubric or agreement statistics, and specific Chat-3D-v2 reproduction details are removed. With the central experiments unchanged, the net improvement is useful but modest.
